questions.question: Your model scores 99% on training data and 62% on test data. What is happening and what do you do?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you recognise overfitting and can name concrete remedies rather than just the word.

questions.question: Why do you need a test set at all? Why not evaluate on the data you trained on?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you genuinely understand generalisation. This is the question that separates tutorial-followers from people who think.

questions.question: Your fraud detector is 99% accurate. Why might that be terrible?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you spot class imbalance and know to reach for precision, recall and the confusion matrix.

questions.question: What is data leakage, and how might it sneak into a project without you noticing?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you have been burned by it - scaling before splitting is the classic example.

questions.question: What does a p-value actually tell you, and what does it not tell you?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you can state it carefully. Most candidates overclaim here, and interviewers know it.

questions.question: When would you report the median instead of the mean?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you think about skew and outliers in real data rather than treating averages as interchangeable.

questions.question: Two variables correlate strongly. What can and cannot you conclude?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you can discuss confounding variables concretely, not just say 'correlation is not causation'.

questions.question: When is a neural network the wrong choice for a problem?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you have judgement about data size and interpretability, rather than defaulting to deep learning.

questions.question: Explain backpropagation to someone who knows calculus but not machine learning.
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you understand it as the chain rule applied backwards through the network.

questions.question: Walk me through the steps of a PyTorch training loop.
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you have actually written one. They listen for zeroing gradients, and will ask what happens if you forget.

questions.question: Why do you call model.eval() before validating?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you know dropout and batch normalisation behave differently during training and inference.

questions.question: Why wrap preprocessing and a model in a scikit-learn Pipeline rather than doing the steps separately?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you understand it prevents leakage during cross-validation.

questions.question: What does cross-validation give you that a single train/test split does not?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you understand variance in the estimate, not just that it is 'more accurate'.

questions.question: How do you turn a sentence into something a model can use?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you can walk from tokenisation through bag-of-words to embeddings and say why each step improved on the last.

questions.question: What does it mean for two pieces of text to be 'close' in embedding space?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you understand semantic similarity geometrically, and can mention cosine similarity.

questions.question: Explain what groupby does in Pandas, with an example from your own work.
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you have used it on real data, rather than only in a tutorial notebook.

questions.question: You find missing values in a dataset. What are your options, and how do you choose?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you consider why the data is missing before deciding to drop or impute.

questions.question: You want to show how a value changed over twelve months. What chart, and why not a pie chart?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you choose a chart to fit the question rather than for decoration.

questions.question: How can a chart be technically accurate but still mislead?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you think about truncated axes and scale, which matters when presenting to stakeholders.

questions.question: You are handed a dataset you have never seen. What are your first three steps?
questions.what_they_are_checking: Whether you have a real process - shape, types, missing values, distributions - before jumping to modelling.
